research_question: Explain lunar phases from the Sun-Earth-Moon geometry, distinguish phases from Earth's shadow, and describe the cycle and common misconceptions.

sources.title: Moon Phases
sources.reliability: Government space agency primary educational source
notes: The Moon reflects sunlight rather than producing its own visible light.
The Sun illuminates half the Moon at a time; the visible fraction changes as the Moon orbits Earth.
The eight named phases repeat over a cycle of about 29.5 days.

sources.title: What Are the Moon’s Phases?
notes: Moon phases arise from changing viewing geometry, not from the Moon changing shape.
The new Moon occurs when the illuminated half is turned mostly away from Earth; full Moon occurs when the near side is largely illuminated from our viewpoint.

sources.title: Earth's Moon
notes: The Moon orbits Earth and its changing position relative to the Sun determines the phase observed from Earth.
The Moon's orbit and viewing geometry also explain why it can sometimes be seen in daytime.

sources.title: What are the phases of the Moon?
notes: The lunar phase cycle is a synodic month, measured between repeated alignments with the Sun as seen from Earth.
The cycle lasts roughly 29.5 days, longer than the Moon's sidereal orbit around Earth.
